question: Which of the following writs is issued by a superior court to compel a lower court or a government officer to perform mandatory or purely ministerial duties correctly?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandamus**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mandamus is a **writ issued by a higher court** to compel a lower court or a government officer to perform mandatory or purely ministerial duties correctly.
 
• It ensures that public authorities fulfill their legal duties.
 
 
• It cannot be issued to compel a private individual or body.
 
 
 
• The term Mandamus means "We Command" in Latin.
 
• This writ is a powerful tool for judicial review of administrative actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Habeas Corpus 

 
 
 
 

 
 
• The writ is issued to produce who has been detained before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
 
 
 

 Prohibition
 
 
 
• This writ is issued by the High Court or the Supreme Court to any interior court, or quasi-judicial body prohibiting it from continuing the proceedings in a case, where it has no jurisdiction to try.
 
 
 
 

 Certiorari
 
 
 
• This writ is issued by the Supreme Court or any High Court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court or judicial authority.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Quo

 
warranto

 
 
 
 
• This writ is issued with a view to restraining a person from holding a public office to which he is not entitled.
